author: Muhammed Yasin Yılmaz
status: Research reports / preprints; not peer reviewed

papers.title: Experience-conditioned computation: provenance-aware feedback and execution limits
papers.abstract: We implement provenance-aware feedback, a shared request budget, and experience-conditioned strategy selection. Persistent experience statistics are distinct from weight training. Synthetic table replay tests mechanism behavior, not real-model quality or efficiency. Model, tokenizer, task and feedback identities constrain admissible comparisons.
papers.finding: Experience can influence the choice of future computation through a persistent record. There is no evidence for presenting this effect as general learning or as a gain in real task performance.
papers.limit: The routing groups are heuristic; the outcomes of untried actions cannot be inferred from the logs of chosen actions. A fixed MoE prior is not a learned expert meaning.

papers.title: Insufficiency witnesses in representation search: deterministic equivalence and a negative result
papers.abstract: Witness filtering and direct representation search are equivalent when they share candidate language, order and complete deterministic consistency checking. All 15 finite comparisons yield identical selected representations, predictions and abstentions. Filtering changes some search costs but provides no additional learning information under this contract.
papers.finding: The hypothesis that witness filtering gives a new learning advantage under these conditions was eliminated; the negative result is kept.
papers.limit: The result makes no claim of superiority or equivalence for other information access, open-ended expression generation, approximate consistency or truncated computation budgets.

papers.title: Persistent procedures, transfer and retesting: first separations in learning while living
papers.abstract: Finite affine worlds separate persistence, transfer and budgeted execution of experience-derived procedures. A strong raw-history baseline with the same inference capability matches accuracy. Transferred adaptation knowledge helps within a family and can hurt under shift. Closed-loop retesting is examined as one subproblem rather than a general solution to lifelong learning.
papers.finding: A persistent right answer, inference cost, update transfer and benefit under change are not the same measure; strong baselines limit many first interpretations of superiority.
papers.limit: The function language and the environment families are given. The expected benefit of retesting does not solve the acquisition of a new computational language or general controlled learning.

papers.title: Representation growth, credit assignment to the past and transport of learning state
papers.abstract: We investigate representation growth, delayed credit assignment and transport of learning state across coordinate changes. A fixed expanded representation matches growth on 6,000 cases. Replay and sufficient statistics can preserve obsolete targets. Preserving current predictions under reparameterization does not by itself preserve subsequent learning dynamics.
papers.finding: Equivalence of execution and equivalence of future updates are distinct; the benefit of growth must be judged against the given expression language and the total cost.
papers.limit: The production grammar and the feedback identities are supplied from outside. If an old summary has lost the distinctions of a new feature, there is no universal state-transport transformation.

papers.title: Representation, memory and temporal relations in one lifetime stream
papers.abstract: A joint stream combines representation expansion, regional memory and target change across 24 lives. A fixed expanded baseline matches final accuracy; fewer solves do not establish total efficiency. Label corruption and stale statistics remain negative controls. Temporal prediction with supplied lag features succeeds on informative input but fails after an uninformative training stream shifts.
papers.finding: Components that work separately do not guarantee reliable learning under all the conditions of one life; the informativeness of the data stream is decisive.
papers.limit: Good prediction with supplied lags is not a general discovery of temporal relations or causal structure. The condition from which a later burst of corrupted data was removed is reported separately.

papers.title: Update behaviour acquired from experience: the benefit of transfer and its reversal
papers.abstract: An update matrix learned across source lives is transferred while prediction weights are reset. Identical initial predictions can therefore lead to different future learning curves. Transfer helps in the same geometry and hurts under reversal; continued adaptation only partly repairs the damage. A separate moment-based risk calculation checks the interpretation.
papers.finding: Experience can change how learning will happen in the future; this capacity cannot be measured from a fixed initial answer, and it can carry its own harm under distribution change.
papers.limit: A small linear geometry and an externally given meta-update family are used. Because it matches IDBD and related literature, no new general learning principle is claimed.

papers.title: A recurrent state procedure acquired from experience, and a memory for relearning
papers.abstract: Finite transition graphs acquired from binary strings are tested on long unseen strings, fresh-process continuation and later relearning. Clean conditions generalize, while a strong bounded enumeration baseline has fewer online errors. Corrupted labels induce larger, poorly generalizing graphs. Compact execution state does not remove the archive used for subsequent learning.
papers.finding: An executable state procedure can be acquired from experience; execution memory, learning memory and the knowledge needed to diagnose an error are different things.
papers.limit: The evaluation of the empty string and that of non-empty languages are reported separately. Correction with true labels supplied from outside does not count as self-diagnosis of errors.

papers.title: Correctable learning state: the limit of today's complete candidate set
papers.abstract: Two histories with the same complete current version space can require different nonempty spaces after the same valid correction. Violation multiplicities match replay when truthful old contents are supplied, with zero mismatches over 1,507,050 projected class-correction cases. Histograms also match. ID-only edits and expanding hypothesis languages expose additional information requirements.
papers.finding: Keeping all of today's consistent candidates is not enough to correct past experience correctly tomorrow; the state to be kept depends on the future operations allowed.
papers.limit: The correctness of a correction is an external assumption. Even with a fixed number of counters, bit memory grows with the length of the history. Subclass projections are not independent experimental worlds.

papers.title: The state required by future learning operations: an exact finite audit
papers.abstract: We compare state classes for all Boolean loss queries, observation counts and identity-only label edits on the same finite histories. Length plus signed label differences suffices for all future Boolean loss queries; identity edits impose a separate linear information bound. Exact enumeration checks 61,575 histories, 712,632 label writes and 358,020 appends with no count-formula or replay mismatches.
papers.finding: Unknown future hypotheses do not always require the full histogram. The information required depends on which queries and operations are to be supported, before whether the hypotheses are known.
papers.limit: A fixed finite domain, all Boolean risks and exact correctness are used. A class count is not an efficient encoder or real-world learning performance; the general living-learning question remains open.

papers.title: A multi-directional experimental campaign for learning while living: the first wave
papers.abstract: A first broad campaign compares memory, representation, update behavior and action-produced experience in four local engines. Of 200 catalog entries across ten families, 48 conditional comparisons yielded 3,456 paired outcomes over discovery and untouched confirmation seeds. Thirty claims were supported, nine contradicted and nine inconclusive under the preregistered synthetic decision rule. Strong controls show that learned representation and update behavior can be conditional and harmful under shift; the general living-learning problem remains open.
papers.finding: The campaign maps conditional mechanisms and negative controls rather than discovering a general computational principle. Experience can change later computation in these supplied languages, but a stronger pre-supplied representation or a shifted environment can remove the apparent advantage.
papers.limit: The worlds, languages, actions, metrics and candidate families are finite and researcher supplied. Catalog entries overlap and are not 200 independent mechanisms. The results are local synthetic evidence, not external peer review, biological validation, AGI evidence or proof of novelty.

papers.title: Cevahir Zihin: a Living Evidence Mind
papers.abstract: A learning system with no neural network, weight matrix, embedding or gradient: whatever it perceives becomes a unit, every relation a tie that keeps graded evidence for and against it per origin, read by one rule (the NARS expectation, k = 1) and learned at every moment, with the evidence of any single experience exactly retractable. On this core 75 mechanisms were built and measured one at a time. Having watched about 1,090 published SCAN training commands twice, it answers all six published SCAN test files exactly (26,227 of 26,227); COGS stays at 0 with its causes measured. On 13,290 Turkish sentences it says a read sentence for 146 to 151 of 200 two-word cues after one reading, a 7.3M-parameter Transformer after an hour of training for 47. A grounded layer answers who does what in situations never described 48 and 54 of 72 (Turkish, English) against 29 and 42 for a Transformer given the scene.
papers.finding: Evidence accounting with one reading rule gives learning without a training phase, without interference and with exact retraction, and compositional generalisation wherever an answer is made of the replies its parts were lived with; the mechanisms that examine and extend the mind itself are switches measured with their failures.
papers.limit: The worlds are small and generated, the Transformer baselines small and trained on one processor, a frame generalises one place (COGS), the cost of the whole mind grows with what it holds, and the grounded world gives its features as opaque codes. Not peer reviewed; no claim of general intelligence.
